stable.title: Dollar wallet
stable.intro: Hold your balance in {{ticker}}, a digital dollar on the Spark network, so bitcoin swings do not reach it.
stable.toggleHint: Turning it on converts your current bitcoin balance. Turning it off converts it back.

stable.custody: Your keys stay on this device. Conversions are signed here, and Voltz neither holds nor moves your funds.
stable.rewardsIssuer: From 3.5% to 6% a year, rising with Flashnet's volume. Paid in bitcoin every day at midnight UTC, straight to your wallet, as long as you hold at least 10 {{ticker}}. Voltz takes no part and no cut.

useDomain.siteNote:
For the Lightning address to work on {{domain}} without taking the site down:

Forward (proxy) only the path /.well-known/lnurlp/ to {{target}}, preserving the original Host header.

Everything else on the site stays as it is. No other path should be forwarded.

deleteData.whatGoes: This deletes from Voltz the address {{address}} and this wallet's other names, the devices that get notifications, the payments received at the address and the comments from people who paid.
deleteData.whatGoesNoAddress: This deletes from Voltz this wallet's names, the devices that get notifications, the payments received at the address and the comments from people who paid.
deleteData.wallet: Your wallet, your bitcoin and the history stay on this device and on the Spark network, and Voltz has no way to delete them.
deleteData.walletThenRemove: Your bitcoin and the history stay on the Spark network, and this wallet's recovery phrase opens them again. This wallet leaves this device once Voltz has the request.
deleteData.contacts: Your contacts stay in the wallet too.
deleteData.passkeyIos: This wallet's passkey stays in the Passwords app, where only you can delete it.
deleteData.passkeyAndroid: This wallet's passkey stays in your phone's password manager, where only you can delete it.
deleteData.paid: Paid names and domain years are lost. Bought less than 14 days ago? Ask for a refund first.
deleteData.refundStore: Ask the store for a refund
deleteData.refundSupport: Ask support for a refund (paid in sats)
deleteData.owedTitle: Charges in sats to sort out with support. Keep each reference before you delete.
deleteData.owedRefused: {{subject}}, {{sats}} sats, on {{date}}: paid, and the purchase was refused. If these sats have not come back to this wallet, support pays them back.
deleteData.owedNotGranted: {{subject}}, {{sats}} sats, on {{date}}: paid, and not delivered. If these sats have not come back to this wallet, support pays them back.
deleteData.owedUnchecked: {{subject}}, {{sats}} sats, on {{date}}: Voltz has not confirmed whether this charge was paid. If it was, support pays it back.
deleteData.domainAlone: {{domain}} leaves Voltz. If you want, transfer it first.
deleteData.domain_one: {{domain}} leaves Voltz and {{count}} wallet loses its address on it. If you want, transfer it first.
deleteData.domain_other: {{domain}} leaves Voltz and {{count}} wallets lose their address on it. If you want, transfer it first.
deleteData.nameAfter: The name goes offline and is held for nobody for 90 days, then it is free.
deleteData.staysPurchases: We keep the purchase record (date, amount, the name or domain bought and the payment reference) for as long as tax law requires, usually 5 years.
deleteData.staysMark: We keep a code that does not reveal your wallet, so another device of yours does not recreate the address on its own.
deleteData.staysRequest: We keep the record of this request, for as long as the purchases, as proof that it was carried out.
deleteData.staysOther: We keep one more record, which support explains if you ask.
deleteData.deadline: Usually under an hour, at most 15 days. We tell you here.
deleteData.deadlineThenRemove: Usually under an hour, at most 15 days.
deleteData.blockedTitle: This can't be deleted yet. Wait for what is in progress to finish.
deleteData.blockerCharge: A charge in sats is still open.
deleteData.blockerStoreOrder: A store order is still open.
deleteData.blockerCredit: A name credit is still reserved.
deleteData.blockerClosing: A name or domain of this wallet is being closed right now.
deleteData.blockerDomainPayment: A domain year of this wallet is being paid.
deleteData.blockerOther: Something on this wallet is still in progress.
deleteData.confirmBody: This can't be undone. Your wallet and your bitcoin stay on this device.
deleteData.confirmBodyThenRemove: This can't be undone. Once Voltz has the request, this wallet leaves this device. Your bitcoin stays where it is, and only this wallet's recovery phrase opens it again.
deleteData.inProgress: Request in progress. We tell you here when it is done.
deleteData.staysUntilConfirmed: Voltz hasn't confirmed the request yet, so this wallet is still on this device. Once Voltz has it, Remove wallet with the option to also delete your data turned on finishes the removal.
deleteData.failed: Couldn't ask right now. Nothing was deleted.
deleteData.checking: Couldn't check this wallet with Voltz right now. Try again later.
deleteData.notArrived: The request didn't reach Voltz. Nothing was deleted.

withdrawal.consent: If Apple asks about this purchase, I allow Voltz to tell Apple that I agree to share this, that the purchase was delivered and works, that no free sample or trial came before it, and that Voltz prefers a full refund.
withdrawal.receipt: Cancellation received on {{date}} at {{time}}. Keep this receipt.
withdrawal.receiptApple: Apple now asks for a reason and decides on the refund. Once you send the request, Apple says to expect an update within 24 to 48 hours.
withdrawal.receiptGoogle: Voltz has already asked Google Play for the refund. Google says how long it takes to show up depends on how you paid.
withdrawal.receiptSats: Your sats are refunded to this wallet within 3 business days.
withdrawal.waitingGoogle: Cancellation requested on {{date}}. Voltz asked Google Play for the refund.
withdrawal.waitingSats: Cancellation requested on {{date}}. Your sats are refunded to this wallet within 3 business days of the request.
withdrawal.refunded: Refunded on {{date}}. {{item}} is no longer yours.
withdrawal.declinedApple: Apple did not approve the refund for this purchase.
withdrawal.failedGoogle: Google Play did not complete the refund. Voltz has been alerted and will finish it by hand.
withdrawal.appleClosed: You closed Apple's request before sending it.
withdrawal.appleDuplicate: Apple already has a refund request for this purchase.
withdrawal.appleFailed: Apple's request could not be opened.
withdrawal.otherWallet: This purchase belongs to another wallet. Open the wallet that paid for it and try there.
withdrawal.noRefundAddress: This wallet's address for the sats could not be read. The request was not sent.
withdrawal.unknownNetwork: Could not reach Voltz. Check your connection and try again.
withdrawal.unknown: The request could not be confirmed. Try again.
withdrawal.unknownPurchase: Voltz does not find this purchase in this wallet.
withdrawal.notWithdrawable: This purchase can no longer be cancelled.
withdrawal.windowClosed: The 14 days to cancel this purchase are over.
withdrawal.creditReserved: The credit from this purchase is in use right now. Try again in a few minutes.
withdrawal.tooMany: Too many requests in a short time. Try again in a few minutes.
withdrawal.refused: Voltz did not accept the request.
withdrawal.payLineApple: You can cancel within 14 days by asking Apple for a refund here. Apple decides.
withdrawal.payLineGoogle: You can cancel within 14 days. Google Play refunds you through the payment method you used.
withdrawal.payLineSats: You can cancel within 14 days and get your sats back.
withdrawal.lapsedApple: Apple sent no word about this request within 14 days, so it was closed. The purchase is still yours.
withdrawal.appleElsewhere: This purchase was made in the App Store. To cancel it, make the request from an iPhone with this wallet or on Apple's refund page.

updateNotice.title: New version of Voltz
updateNotice.body: Install it through your device's store when you can.
updateNotice.criticalBody: We recommend installing the latest version today, through your device's store.

passkey.explain: A passkey is a digital key used instead of a password. Deleting it without your words can lose the wallet.
passkey.didNotOpen: The passkey did not open. If you already have one, try again. If not, create a new one.
passkey.noCredential: No passkey found for Voltz. Use your words below.
passkey.unavailable: Passkeys are not available here. Use your words.
passkey.failed: The passkey did not work this time.
passkey.wordsOwed: Your device did not say this passkey syncs to your account, so write down these words before going on.
passkey.synced: Your device says this passkey syncs to your account.
passkey.deleteIos: Removing this wallet does not delete its passkey. To delete it, open the Passwords app.
passkey.deleteAndroid: Removing this wallet does not delete its passkey. To delete it, open your phone's password manager.

recoverableFunds.title: Funds outside your balance
recoverableFunds.body: There may be up to {{amount}} sats outside your balance.
recoverableFunds.staleBody: There may be up to {{amount}} sats outside your balance. This figure is from the last reading and may be out of date.

emergencyExit.title: Emergency exit
emergencyExit.homeUnderWay: Your emergency exit is under way. Tap to follow it.
emergencyExit.homeArrives: After fees, {{amount}} arrives at the address you chose.
emergencyExit.homeArrivesAtLeast: After fees, at least {{amount}} arrives at the address you chose.
emergencyExit.homeWaits: Your emergency exit is waiting for you. Tap to see what it needs.
emergencyExit.removeRefused: This wallet has an emergency exit under way. Wait for it to finish before you remove the wallet.
emergencyExit.unreadable: Could not read your emergency exit on this device.
emergencyExit.aside: An earlier exit could not be read and was kept apart. Your funds stay recoverable by starting a new exit.
emergencyExit.networkUpBody: You can use Send as usual, which is cheaper and arrives sooner. The emergency exit is for when the network stops answering.
emergencyExit.introAll: For emergencies only: this takes your bitcoin out of the Spark network, directly onto Bitcoin. Tokens such as USDB and DePix do not leave this way.
emergencyExit.introDays: It takes weeks, about two to four, and no one can say the exact day, because each step waits for blocks.
emergencyExit.introFee: You need bitcoin from another wallet to pay the network fees.
emergencyExit.introOpen: Open the app every 8 hours or so while it runs. That keeps the fee as quoted. After longer, part of the fee can come out of what you receive.
emergencyExit.introDevice: It works on the device that synced this wallet. On a new device it needs the network back.
emergencyExit.introOtherDevice: Until the exit ends, do not open this wallet on another device, with its words or its passkey.
emergencyExit.destinationLabel: Bitcoin address that receives the funds
emergencyExit.destinationHint: Use an address from another wallet of yours.
emergencyExit.destinationBad: This is not a Bitcoin address.
emergencyExit.destinationUri: Paste only the address, with nothing around it.
emergencyExit.destinationOwn: This is this wallet's own address. Use one from another wallet.
emergencyExit.destinationUnchecked: Could not check this address. Make sure it comes from another wallet.
emergencyExit.quoteFailed: Could not work out the exit right now.
emergencyExit.noRate: Could not read the network fee right now.
emergencyExit.nothing: There is no bitcoin to move this way.
emergencyExit.nothingFee: The network fee today is higher than what there is to move. Try again when fees fall.
emergencyExit.nothingData: This device does not have what it needs to move these funds yet.
emergencyExit.nothingOperators: The network did not answer, so these funds could not be found yet. Try again later.
emergencyExit.reviewLeftover: Whatever the fees do not use from your payment arrives at the same address.
emergencyExit.notWorth: The network fees are as high as the amount or higher, so moving it now costs more than it returns.
emergencyExit.tooSmall: This amount is too small for the Bitcoin network to carry, so it would not arrive.
emergencyExit.thin: Network fees take more than a fifth of this amount.
emergencyExit.startFailed: Could not build the exit. Nothing was sent, and your payment stays at the address.
emergencyExit.startFailedNoFee: Could not build the exit. Nothing was sent.
emergencyExit.requoted: The network fee changed, so this is a new quote.
emergencyExit.operatorsDown: The network could not sign this exit. Nothing was sent. Try again later.
emergencyExit.fundBody: From another wallet, send at least {{amount}} sats to this address in one payment, and wait for it to confirm.
emergencyExit.fundUnread: Could not read it right now.
emergencyExit.fundShort: {{amount}} sats are missing. Send them to this address from another wallet.
emergencyExit.fundShortNoFigure: The fee is still short. Send more to this address from another wallet.
emergencyExit.fundShortWait: A payment is on its way to this address. Wait for it to confirm.
emergencyExit.trackBody: Keep opening the app every 8 hours or so. Each step goes out when its turn comes.
emergencyExit.trackWaiting: The next step can go from block {{height}}.
emergencyExit.trackOffline: No connection. Your exit stays as it was.
emergencyExit.trackStuck: Could not update the exit right now. The app tries again at the next check.
emergencyExit.trackAwaitingRead: One step is waiting until the network can be read.
emergencyExit.trackCopyHint: You can take these transactions to a Bitcoin node that accepts them as a pair.
emergencyExit.trackFailedLeaves: Part of the funds stayed out of this exit and needs another one.
emergencyExit.payMoreTop: This exit already pays the fastest fee.
emergencyExit.payMoreFailed: Could not raise the fee right now.
emergencyExit.askTitleRedo: This exit has to be built again
emergencyExit.askBody: These are the new figures. Nothing goes out until you confirm.
emergencyExit.askNeeded: This exit has to be built again, and its figures changed.
emergencyExit.askLaterBody: The app stops following this exit here. Your funds stay recoverable by starting a new exit.
emergencyExit.doneBody: Every step confirmed on the Bitcoin network.
emergencyExit.doneLeft: {{amount}} sats stayed at the fee address. Your words and passphrase open them in any wallet that uses BIP84.
emergencyExit.donePending: {{amount}} sats are on their way to the fee address.
emergencyExit.doneUnread: Could not check what stayed at the fee address.
emergencyExit.closedLater: This exit stopped here. Your funds stay recoverable by starting a new exit.
emergencyExit.fundShortOneCoin: This address holds many small payments, and the network does not take them all in one transaction. Send {{amount}} sats or more to it in a single payment from another wallet.
emergencyExit.sendHeld: This wallet has an emergency exit under way. Sending waits until it finishes.
emergencyExit.sendHeldUnread: Could not read this wallet's emergency exit. Sending waits until it can be read.
emergencyExit.receiveHeld: This wallet has an emergency exit under way. Receiving waits until it finishes.
emergencyExit.receiveHeldUnread: Could not read this wallet's emergency exit. Receiving waits until it can be read.
emergencyExit.balanceUnread: Could not read this wallet's emergency exit. This balance may still count what the exit is moving.
emergencyExit.balanceHeld: While the emergency exit runs, this wallet sends nothing and gives out no address to receive. Part of this balance may be leaving through the exit.
emergencyExit.spendHeld: This wallet has an emergency exit under way. Payments and conversions wait until it finishes.
emergencyExit.spendHeldUnread: Could not read this wallet's emergency exit. Payments and conversions wait until it can be read.
